newsitem.title: USA: Newspaper advertising makes best showing in 10 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper advertising makes best showing in 10 yrs.

text.p: Advertising revenue for the first quarter of 1997 injected $8.9 billion into the newspaper industry, an increase of nearly nine percent over the same period last year, the Newspaper Association of America said on Thursday.

The increase marked the best single quarterly showing for the industry in 10 years and was hailed by NAA president and chief executive John Sturm as an indication of "the underlying strength of the newspaper industry.

"Most importantly," Sturm said in a statement, "advertisers recognize the proven value of newspapers as an advertising vehicle and that is reflected in the continuing growth in total newspaper advertising revenues."

First quarter results show classified advertising up 9.8 percent to $3.5 billion. Retail advertising grew by 7.1 percent to $4.2 billion and national advertising rose 12.7 percent to $1.2 billion, the NAA said.
NAA is a nonprofit organization representing the $46 billion newspaper industry and more than 1,600 newspapers in the U.S. and Canada.
